\subsection*{Util --- Stable Pass: Introduction}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Programs.Util.StablePass}.

\subsection*{Util --- Stable Pass: Results}

\begin{definition}[Key at a list position]
\lean{Light.keyAt}
\label{Light.keyAt}
\leanok
For a key function $k:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, a list $\pi$ of natural numbers, and an
index $j$, the key at position $j$ is $k$ applied to the list entry there, using $0$ as
the entry when $j$ is out of range.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Key at a list index]
\lean{Light.keyAt_eq}
\label{Light.keyAt_eq}
\leanok
\uses{Light.keyAt}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\pi$ be a list of natural numbers, let $kd:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$, and let
$j<|\pi|$. The value of $kd$ at the entry of $\pi$ indexed by $j$ is $kd(\pi_j)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Stable sorting pass]
\lean{Light.IsStablePass}
\label{Light.IsStablePass}
\leanok
\uses{Light.keyAt, Light.sortPos}
For a key function $k:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ and lists $\pi,\pi\prime$ of natural
numbers, $\pi\prime$ is a stable pass of $\pi$ when the lists have the same length and,
for every index $j<|\pi|$, the item $\pi_j$ appears in $\pi\prime$ at the position
given by sorting items by key $k$ and preserving their original order when keys tie.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Permutation from a stable pass]
\lean{Light.IsStablePass.perm}
\label{Light.IsStablePass.perm}
\leanok
\uses{Light.IsStablePass, Light.eq_of_sortPos_eq, Light.keyAt, Light.sortPos, Light.sortPos_lt}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\pi,\pi'$ be lists of natural numbers and let $k$ assign a natural-number key to
each natural number. Suppose $\pi'$ has the same length as $\pi$ and, for every index
$j$ within $\pi$, its entry at position $r_j$ is $\pi_j$, where $r_j$ is the number of
entries of $\pi$ with key strictly less than the key of $\pi_j$, plus the number of
occurrences of that same key among the entries before position $j$. Then $\pi'$ is a
permutation of $\pi$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sorted keys after a stable pass]
\lean{Light.IsStablePass.sorted}
\label{Light.IsStablePass.sorted}
\leanok
\uses{Light.IsStablePass, Light.exists_sortPos_eq, Light.keyAt, Light.keyAt_eq, Light.sortPos, Light.sortPos_lt_sortPos_iff}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\pi,\pi'$ be lists of natural numbers, let $k,d$ be functions from natural numbers
to natural numbers, and let $B$ be a natural number. Suppose $\pi'$ has the same length
as $\pi$ and places each entry of $\pi$ at the position given by the number of entries
with smaller $k$-key plus the number of earlier entries with equal $k$-key. Assume also
that $g(i)<B$ for every entry $i$ of $\pi$, and that the values of $g$ along $\pi$ are
nondecreasing. Then the values $k(i)B+g(i)$ along $\pi'$ are nondecreasing.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Threshold count for list keys]
\lean{Light.cntLt_keyAt}
\label{Light.cntLt_keyAt}
\leanok
\uses{Light.cntLt, Light.cntLt_congr, Light.cntLt_succ_right, Light.keyAt}
\difficulty{4}
Let $kd:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, let $\pi$ be a finite list of natural numbers, and let
$s\in\mathbb{N}$. The number of positions in the list whose key under $kd$ is less than
$s$ equals the number of list entries $i$ for which $kd(i)<s$.
\end{theorem}
